key_insight: Homogenized stress becomes a one-local quantum observable, measurable from the same computational-basis samples as the two-local Ising energy without reconstructing microscopic displacements.
engineering_relevance: The formulation offers a quantum route to extracting effective stresses from linear-elastic representative volume elements for multiscale mechanics.
method: Encode reduced finite-element RVE energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate the equilibrium ground state using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Differentiate the strain-dependent Hamiltonian via Hellmann–Feynman to obtain stress observables containing only identity and single-qubit Pauli-Z terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE, but provides no quantitative accuracy, hardware, or speedup results.
watch_item: Stress accuracy depends on the finite encoding grid and VQE state quality; the one-local result relies on strain-independent couplings in linear elasticity.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
